title: Accounts Receivable Policy for Continuum Backup & Recovery — Payments, Late Fees and Suspension for Non-Payment
content:
Invoices on a Continuum Backup & Recovery plan fall due the tier's net payment days after posting; payments apply to the named invoice, otherwise oldest first, one entry per invoice. On the first day of each month every invoice unpaid more than the tier's grace days after its due date is assessed one late fee of the tier's monthly late fee percentage of its unpaid balance, rounded half up to the cent. New backups pause once the oldest unpaid invoice is the tier's suspension threshold of days past due, existing restore points being kept, and resume once all past-due invoices are paid; after the tier's termination threshold of days in suspension the plan may be terminated for non-payment.

## The amount owed

The plan's balance due is the amount the client owes on the plan: charges increase it and payments reduce it. Monthly fees, the onboarding fee, restore labor charges, failover overage charges, late fees and early termination fees are charges; a payment applied to an invoice reduces it.

## Applying a payment

| Payment received | How it is applied |
|---|---|
| Names an invoice | To the named invoice |
| Names no invoice | To unpaid invoices oldest first |

Each invoice a payment reaches is recorded as its own entry: a remittance spread over several invoices produces one entry per invoice.

**Example (hypothetical figures only).** A client owes an older invoice of 400.00 USD and a newer invoice of 300.00 USD and sends 500.00 USD naming no invoice. 400.00 USD is applied to the older invoice and 100.00 USD to the newer one, as two entries; 200.00 USD of the newer invoice remains unpaid.

## Late fees

On the first day of each month, each invoice that is still unpaid more than the grace days after its due date is assessed one late fee for that month, equal to the monthly late fee percentage of that invoice's unpaid balance, rounded half up to the cent.

**Example (hypothetical figures only).** On a hypothetical tier with a 5-day grace period and a 1.5 percent monthly late fee, an invoice fell due 12 days before the first day of the month and has 250.00 USD unpaid. On the first day of the month it is unpaid more than 5 days after its due date, so one late fee of 1.5 percent of 250.00 USD, that is 3.75 USD, is assessed for that month.

## Suspension and termination for non-payment

| Plan status | What it means |
|---|---|
| suspended | New backups are paused for non-payment; existing restore points are retained |
| active (after reinstatement) | Backups resume after the past-due balance is cleared |
| closed (terminated for non-payment) | The plan is terminated for non-payment |

| Point reached | Effect |
|---|---|
| The oldest unpaid invoice reaches the tier's suspension threshold of days past due | New backups pause; existing restore points are kept |
| All past-due invoices are paid | Backups resume |
| The plan has been in suspension for the tier's termination threshold of days | The plan may be terminated for non-payment |

**Timeline (hypothetical figures only).** On a hypothetical tier with a 30-day suspension threshold and a 30-day termination threshold, new backups pause on the day the oldest unpaid invoice is 30 days past due. If every past-due invoice is then paid, backups resume. If not, once the plan has been in suspension for 30 days it may be terminated for non-payment; the termination is permitted at that point, not automatic.
